Cookery Rules & Food Preservation

Cooking methods, nutrient loss during cooking, and food preservation methods.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List cooking methods and their effects on nutrients
  • Describe ways to minimize nutrient loss
  • Explain food preservation methods

In simple words

Cooking makes food safe, tasty and digestible, but it can also destroy nutrients. Using the right cooking methods preserves nutrients.

Food preservation keeps food safe to eat for longer by stopping or slowing the growth of microbes.

Cooking methods

Method Effect on nutrients
Steaming Best; minimal nutrient loss
Pressure cooking Good; fast, less water
Boiling Some water-soluble vitamins lost
Frying Adds fat; some nutrient loss
Roasting/Baking Some vitamin loss

Minimizing nutrient loss

  • Wash vegetables before cutting, not after.
  • Cut into large pieces; cook soon after cutting.
  • Use minimum water; do not overcook.
  • Use the cooking water in soups or gravies (it contains leached vitamins).
  • Avoid adding baking soda to vegetables (destroys vitamin C).

Food preservation methods

  • Drying/sun-drying — removes water; microbes cannot grow.
  • Refrigeration — slows microbial growth.
  • Freezing — stops most microbial growth.
  • Canning — heat-sealed; long shelf life.
  • Salting and sugaring — draw out water; preserve.
  • Pasteurization — heat treatment of milk to kill germs.

🔴 Steaming preserves nutrients

Steaming and pressure cooking best preserve nutrients. Wash vegetables before cutting, use minimum water, and do not overcook.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Patient meals — advise gentle cooking to preserve nutrients in therapeutic diets.
  • Health teaching — teach families to wash before cutting, avoid excess oil, and not overcook.
  • Food storage — store cooked food properly; reheat only once.
  • Milk safety — advise pasteurized or boiled milk.
  • Infection control — ensure kitchen hygiene and safe food handling.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Cooking makes food safe and digestible but can destroy nutrients.
  2. Steaming and pressure cooking best preserve nutrients.
  3. Wash vegetables before cutting; use minimum water; do not overcook.
  4. Food preservation: drying, refrigeration, freezing, canning, salting, pasteurization.
  5. Pasteurization kills germs in milk by heat treatment.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Water-soluble vitamins (B, C) are lost in cooking water.
  2. Baking soda destroys vitamin C — avoid adding it.
  3. Reheat cooked food only once.
  4. Store cooked food covered and at safe temperatures.

📌 Memory trick

Cook to save nutrients: “W-C-M-N” — Wash before Cutting, Minimum water, No overcooking.

60-second revision

  • Cooking preserves nutrients best by steaming and pressure cooking.
  • Wash before cutting; minimum water; no overcooking.
  • Avoid baking soda (destroys vitamin C).
  • Preservation: drying, refrigeration, freezing, canning, salting, pasteurization.
  • Reheat cooked food only once.

Test yourself

Which cooking method best preserves nutrients?

Answer: C. Steaming uses little water and heat, best preserving nutrients.

Vegetables should be washed:

Answer: B. Washing before cutting prevents loss of water-soluble vitamins.

Baking soda added to vegetables destroys:

Answer: B. Baking soda destroys vitamin C in vegetables.

Pasteurization is:

Answer: B. Pasteurization heats milk to kill harmful germs.

Cooked food should be reheated:

Answer: B. Reheat cooked food only once to reduce microbial risk.
